source: WriteStallTimeoutHandler closes an HTTP/2 connection whose client opened every flow-control window and then took none of the bytes waiting for it for responseWriteStallTimeoutMillis (the socket, not a window, holds the response back, so no stream is reset), and counts it in mock_server_response_write_stalls_total{protocol=http2,scope=connection} (MetricsTest#countsResponseWriteStallsUnderTheirProtocolAndScope). logLevel WARN keeps the tens of MB out of the event log, whose rendering starved the timed scenarios replayed in the same process

steps.note: a 30 MB response on an HTTP/2 connection with every window open whose client stops reading: the connection is closed, without a reset or GOAWAY, before the response ends

mask.reason: only the series this scenario drives; the rest are pinned by metrics.json

steps.note: the WARN, with the bytes waiting for the client when it was cut

mask.reason: the 30 MB response, logged when it was returned

Netty's ChannelOutboundBuffer.totalPendingWriteBytes (the unwritten messages plus 96 bytes of entry overhead each: 32864 for one 32 KiB slice of PacedLargeWriteHandler, 30000096 for a 30 MB binary answer written whole) against the rest of the write our socket has not taken, which depends on socket buffers
